boxes.meaning: cause, make something end up a certain way

english.note: Use this colloquial choice when emphasizing the resulting situation, especially an unwanted one.
Use 搞到 when cost means causing someone to lose something, suffer, or end up in trouble rather than simply naming a price.
Use this when an action or situation causes someone or something to end up in a state or causes a result, including making someone cry.
Use this colloquial phrase when an action or event causes a situation or consequence, especially an undesirable one.
Use this colloquial causative when something makes a person end up in a changed or usually bad state, such as going mad.
Use 搞到 when putting someone or something into a resulting state or condition, especially in casual speech.

examples.english: That mistake can cause me to lose sleep all night.
examples.traditional: 呢個錯誤搞到我成晚瞓唔着。
